correctness.rationale: The degree-based first-force proof confines each optimal 3-set to a 3-column end strip for all n>=5. Restriction to the 5-column prefix is necessary for any long-grid success; a complete 84-case local test yields exactly thirteen left seeds. Each has a <=5-round history filling all first three columns before touching the fourth; column sweeps extend to every n>=5. A separate exact intersection-graph check yields 24 edges, radius 3, diameter 5 for each of two disconnected components. Independent set-based and bit-mask verifiers replay exact n=3..10 counts. Finite computations alone are not used for the infinite claim.

value.rationale: The discovery supplies a sharp reconfiguration connectivity threshold for an infinite, natural Cartesian grid family, with an explicit optimum-state classification and the full invariant 13-vertex component. Under a no-extra-sensor exchange rule, the end-local rigidity identifies precisely why relocating an optimum initial forcing set between opposite ends is impossible once n>=5. This is structural and not a numerical isolated census; its exact nature invites comparisons with wider strips or variants, without claiming those results.
